assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the two reviewed items curated on tomozaki:hinami-nagisa@light-novel at basis_commit, each read in full: #bounded-character-dossier, the canonical B-scope Hinami Nagisa bounded posthumous character dossier (INDEPENDENT_BOUNDED_LITERARY_SCOPE_PASS, scope B_STRICTLY_ATTRIBUTED_POSTHUMOUS), whose evidence register is HN-E01 to HN-E10 in Japanese V08.5, V10, V11 and V12, all retrospective, reported, survivor-interior or fiction/address routes; and #attributed-retrieval-model, the canonical derived-use attributed retrieval/constraint model (NG1 to NG5), marked do_not_use_as_primary_literary_authority, which derives from the dossier, enacts no interior and is not used as literary evidence. The project's current-state entrypoint was read for method and gate state only. The supporting character implementation review, the supporting literary evidence manifest, the historical and context retrieval integration review, operator guide and packet, the readings and the ledgers (CS section 13.6/19, CRI-HIN-005, REL-C10) are not curated on this subject and are not evidence here. No adaptation, performed voice, reception or post-V12 material is in scope.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Nagisa's own life as retrospectively represented in three bands: the childhood play state (V08.5 HN-E01/E02), the early intervention state and the distressed questioning state (V11 HN-E03 to HN-E05), ending before her death, whose mechanism and intent are unknown; the V10, V11 and V12 death reports and the V12 imagined reunion are survivor reports and fiction/address, not later Nagisa states. Exact age and school year are unreconciled (V10 sixth grade versus V11 fourth grade).
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The dossier gives a bounded account of her expressed reasons: a stated correctness rationale borrowed from the game phrase, reassurance performed under visible strain, and a later question whether that phrase can still address her condition (sections 3 and 4, HN-E03 to HN-E05); the model retrieves these as NG2 and NG3 and refuses to simulate new crisis decisions. D is rejected because her own conduct rests on one childhood game and one V11 retrospective history, the representation is not a verbatim record, her final state of mind is explicitly unavailable, and no mechanism is tested beyond those episodes. NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because her expressed reasons and their change are located.

The dossier and model separate three bands with a represented change between them: childhood play (HN-E01), early intervention under advice (HN-E03/E04), and the distressed question whether doing right had meaning (HN-E05), which the dossier calls a consequential change in her own account; NG3 requires reassurance, exhaustion and doubt to keep different dates. C is rejected because the bands are retrospective episodes inside Aoi's disclosure, their exact school years conflict (V10 P139 against V11 P826-842), and the last state before her death is unknown. E is rejected because an evidenced change of belief across located bands is more than a single local state.

The discovery row does not claim SPEECH. A few utterances are located in retrospective scenes (wanting a rematch, saying the game is fun, insisting she is all right, asking whether Buin could still say the line), but the dossier states that V11 dialogue is not a verbatim heard transcript and the model awards no new Japanese dialogue, complete idiolect or acoustics. D is rejected because no register features are described; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the utterances and their non-verbatim status are located.

Ordinary conduct is one represented childhood game (V08.5 part0013 P1-57: loss, rematch, two-bomb timing change, win, thanking Haruka, approaching Aoi) and remembered three-sister play (part0015 P188-213), plus a report at the family meal. D is rejected because the dossier explicitly refuses favorites, a gaming identity or standing habits and no other routine is shown; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the play acts are paragraph-located.

The dossier's section 6 table separates Aoi as play rival, Haruka as cheering sister, the targeted classmate, the perpetrating classmates, Yoko as adviser, Aoi addressed in distress and later readers; the model's directional standing keeps Aoi in play distinct from Aoi in distress. C is rejected because each recipient rests on one or two retrospective episodes, conduct toward the classmate and perpetrators reaches the reader only through her own reports, and no recipient-conditioned behavior is modeled beyond retrieval. E is rejected because recipient-specific acts and limits are explicitly tabulated.

Her expressed doubt and her wish to help are rendered as historical speech; the inward narration of V11 and V12 is Aoi's, and her last interior is explicitly unavailable (V10 part0024/part0026, V12 p0022 P504-514). D is rejected because no interior of hers is directly rendered beyond retrospective speech; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the evidence explicitly characterizes what is and is not accessible.

She proposes cautioning the perpetrators, later reports cautioning them again and bearing retaliation (HN-E04), and competes in play; no confrontation of hers is depicted as a scene, and the dossier says efficacy and class dynamics are unestablished. D is rejected because the conflict conduct is reported rather than shown and rests on one history; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the reported acts are located.

Her own normative sequence is located: she names a classmate's mistreatment as intolerable, asks her mother what she can do, proposes cautioning the others, acts despite Yoko's suggestion that watching is an option, gives the correctness rationale, and later asks whether doing right had meaning (HN-E03 to HN-E05, dossier sections 3 and 4). C is rejected because the weighing behind the choice is not rendered, the account is retrospective within one arc, and her final ethical stance is explicitly unknown. E is rejected because these are her own located normative statements with an evidenced change, not only observer judgments.

Play is located in the V08.5 game (celebration, laughter, the declaration that it is fun) and in the sisters' enjoyment of Buin's phrase as repeated playful speech before its later serious use (HN-E01, HN-E04). D is rejected because this is one represented game plus remembered play; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the play acts are located.

An independently reviewed B-scope posthumous dossier with exact member and paragraph windows HN-E01 to HN-E10 across V08.5, V10, V11 and V12, paired with an accepted attributed retrieval model. C is rejected because the account is bounded, every route is retrospective, reported, survivor-interior or fiction/address, and the reviews, manifest, packet, readings and ledgers are not curated on this subject; E is rejected because the dossier is independently reviewed with exact located windows.

Both items state affirmative located limits: final intent, accident or deliberate act and preventability are explicitly unknown in V10 (part0024/part0026) and again in V12 (p0022 P504-514); the V10 sixth-grade and V11 fourth-grade placements conflict; she acts despite maternal caution, so her choice is not obedience; her doubt is not renunciation of help; the V12 reunion is authored address under Kikuchi's stated limit that Nagisa cannot be asked (HN-E09/E10); seven rival accounts are disposed (section 8). B is rejected because the limits rest on a small set of retrospective windows and several are stated unknowns rather than contradictions shown across contexts; D is rejected because these are located, subject-specific limits rather than gap statements.

The dossier separates three clocks (her life, the V08.5/V10/V11 disclosure order and the V12 rereading) and binds each band to exact windows; NG3 and NG4 keep reassurance, doubt and death reports on separate dates. C is rejected because the V10/V11 school-year conflict is preserved unharmonized, so exact age and date reconstruction is blocked, and the bands are episodes rather than dated knowledge states. E is rejected because claims are bound to distinct located bands and disclosure events.

scenario_readiness.note: The model supplies no new first-person voice, no new Japanese dialogue and no idiolect, and the dossier forbids supplying her missing words or final wishes. CONDITIONAL would generate a posthumous voice the evidence explicitly withholds; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the evidence explicitly bounds voice.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One of the three retrospective bands only: the V08.5 childhood play state, the V11 early intervention state or the V11 distressed questioning state, all before her death; nothing after her death is a Nagisa state, and the V12 reunion is fiction/address.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Only attested recipients in their represented standing: Aoi as play rival and affectionate sister or as the sister addressed in distress, Haruka as cheering sister, Yoko as the mother whose advice she seeks, and the targeted and perpetrating classmates as she reports them.
setting_constraints: Family game play, the family meal and the school persecution history as represented only
No road-entry intention, final words, afterlife contact, diagnosis or preventability finding
Output would be attributed retrieval with labeled alternatives, never an enacted posthumous persona or new dialogue

scenario_readiness.note: The model is manual attributed retrieval and places new crisis decisions outside its admission; the dossier requires abstention on what she intended or would endorse after death and calls its era constraints literary, not a validated decision model. CONDITIONAL would enact a deceased child from retrospective episodes; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the evidence explicitly bounds transfer.

Ordinary social conduct is one game and remembered play; the model can retrieve strategy, delight and thanks from that record but enacts no persona. CONDITIONAL would generate ordinary social behavior from one play scene; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the play scene and its limits are located.

Her advice-seeking, chosen intervention and later doubt are located, but the model admits only an ethical comparison by retrieval and puts new crisis decisions outside its field, and her last ethical stance is unknown. CONDITIONAL would invent the deliberation the source leaves unrendered; NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because her located normative acts bound the scenario.
No romantic conduct of Nagisa's appears in the curated items, and neither item models or bounds it. Nothing is established either way.
She is represented as an elementary-school child; no work, role or professional field is in the curated items, and neither item models or bounds one. Nothing is established either way.

known_limits.statement: Whether her road entry was fatigue or dizziness, an accident or a deliberate act, and whether any intervention would have prevented the death, are explicitly unknown in V10 and again after more than five years in V12 (p0022 P504-514); the V11 hospital scene supplies no road viewpoint.
The collision description and the driver's remorse reach the reader through Aoi's report to Fumiya (V10 part0024/part0026), not as a depicted final scene or Nagisa focalization.

V10 part0024 P139 places her in sixth grade when the bullying history begins; V11 p0030 P826-842 makes her two years younger than sixth-grade Aoi and a fourth grader. The conflict is preserved, not harmonized.
She intervenes despite Yoko's suggestion that watching without acting is an option (V11 p0030 P851-906), so her choice is not reducible to following maternal advice.
Her later question whether doing right had meaning (P907-994) establishes doubt and distress, not abandonment of help, loss of love for the classmate or a chosen death.

The V12 imagined reunion and its affirming Nagisa are authored address within Aoi's private reading (p0022 P846-979) under Kikuchi's stated limit that Nagisa can no longer be observed or asked (p0021 P11-149); they are not recovered last words.
All of her conduct is retrospective representation within survivors' disclosure; no living Nagisa scene at a story present exists, and V11 dialogue is not a verbatim heard transcript.
The targeted child's full response, the class structure and adult or school actions are not supplied.
The implementation and integration reviews, manifest, packet, operator guide, readings and ledgers are not curated on this subject.
No idiolect, habitual distribution or acoustic manner is established and generated speech was not evaluated.
